name: background-beams
title: Background Beams
description: A dark backdrop of long curved lines along which short cyan-to-violet gradient segments travel downward on staggered loops. It is meant to sit behind a headline, some copy and an email field.
use: A dark waitlist or hero panel needs faint motion behind centred copy and a field.
avoid: You need a punchy or high-contrast effect: the beams nearly vanish on most screens.
a11y: The decorative SVG is not marked aria-hidden and the endless loops have no reduced-motion check. (keyboard: n-a, labels: n-a, reduced motion: not handled)
looks: A near-black panel with a large pale gradient headline, a block of grey paragraph text and a dark rounded email field holding a grey placeholder. Thin coloured threads in cyan, indigo and violet curve down across the empty space around them.
behaves: Short gradient segments run along long fixed curves, each on its own six-to-twelve second loop with a random start, so a few beams are always sliding downward and fading at either end. Nothing reacts to the pointer.
customise: Only className is exposed. The fifty hardcoded path shapes, their cyan-purple stops and the random loop timings are baked into the file.
weight: moderate: Roughly fifty SVG paths, each animating its own gradient coordinates forever.
demo: Headline "Join the waitlist", a MailJet email-service paragraph and a you@company.com email field.
issues: The beams are faint and sparse, so most of the panel stays as flat black.
polishWhy: A restrained, competent effect, but the threads are so dim that the panel reads almost static.
